project.brief: A 20 second YouTube explainer for Slotly, a scheduling app for small business owners. Calm, clear, modern. The goal is free trial sign-ups. Audience: small business owners who lose hours to back-and-forth booking emails. No footage, no logo file, no voiceover, no music.
project.objective: Drive free trial sign-ups for Slotly, a scheduling app for small business owners
project.audience: Small business owners who lose hours to back-and-forth booking emails

result.rationale: The user wants a new video made and the inventory is empty (no videos, images or audio), so edit_existing and create_full are ruled out. This is a graphics-led create_minimal job. The goal, audience, platform, duration and tone are stated. Aspect ratio was not stated, so it stays null and the application fills the default. YouTube explainer does not state 16:9 explicitly, so I did not guess.

treatment.logline: A small business owner's booking emails pile up, then settle into one calm calendar, and the viewer starts Slotly's 14-day free trial.
treatment.hook: Frame one: a booking email thread already in progress ("Does Tuesday work?" "Actually, can we do Thursday?") stacking up message by message. No logo and no title card.
treatment.tone: Calm, clear, modern, and reassuring. It's a little wry about the email ping-pong, never panicky and never hype.

beats.purpose: Hook. Show the pain concretely: a booking thread of 'what time works?' messages piling up. The viewer thinks 'that's my inbox'.
Turn. Show, as a concept illustration, open time slots with one slot being picked and confirmed. The mess resolves into a single action. No results or time-saved figures are stated.
Reassure. State the approved compatibility fact: works with Google Calendar and Outlook, shown as layered calendar cards.
Conclusion. Hold still on one action: start the free trial, free for 14 days, with the typeset Slotly wordmark.

art_direction.audience_response: Feel the relief of recognising their own email ping-pong, think 'there must be a calmer way to book', and start the free trial.
art_direction.concept: From noise to one clear slot: the film moves from a crowded, overlapping inbox to a single quiet calendar choice, and the layout gets calmer as it goes.
art_direction.visual_metaphor: A tangle of overlapping message bubbles that straightens into one neat row of open time slots, which shows the shift from back-and-forth to a single choice.

typography.rationale: Bold sentence case reads as friendly and plain-spoken for busy owners. Standard scale keeps 16:9 headlines legible without shouting.

art_direction.composition: The headline sits top-left on a wide left-aligned column, and the picture fills the right two-thirds with generous empty space around it. Nothing crosses the safe margins. The final card is centred and uncluttered.

motion_language.description: Slow, smooth pushes and wipes with no bounce. Messages arrive at an even pace and the final card settles and holds.

narrative.opening: Opens on a booking thread already under way, with messages stacking up, so the viewer sees the problem in the first frame.
narrative.development: A calm calendar picks one slot, and then cards show that it works with the calendars owners already use.
narrative.conclusion: A still end card with one button, the free 14-day trial, held long enough to read.

uses.rationale: S01 has a message_thread visual block and no footage, so scene-composition draws the whole scene, including the slow push-in and the overlay. Duration is 5s, inside the recipe's 2-12s range.
The storyboard asks for a crossfade out of the noisy hook into the calm turn. 0.6s is the default and is well under half of the 5s scene.
S02 has a ui_demo visual block (calendar window, cursor, confirmation). scene-composition draws it with no parameters. Duration is 5s, inside range.
A slightly longer soft blend into the reassurance scene suits the calm mood. 0.8s is under half of the 5s scene.
S03 has a layered_cards visual block with parallax and a pull-out, so scene-composition draws it. The overlay is the approved compatibility line. Duration is 4s, inside range.
The storyboard asks for a crossfade into the end card. 0.6s is the default and is under half of the 4s scene.

S04 has an end_card visual block, so scene-composition draws the held end card with the wordmark, headline, button and subline. The end-card-cta recipes are not used, because a visual_block scene takes only scene-composition. Duration is 6s, inside range. S04 is the final scene, so no dip-to-black is planned. That recipe is only required on non-final scenes, and there is no following scene to dip into. The storyboard's dip_to_black on S04 is therefore not planned, and the final fade needs a decision if it is wanted.
